newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian police minister claims police harrassment.
newsitem.headline: Australian police minister claims police harrassment.

text.p: A former Australian state police minister has complained that he was forced to quit the post after receiving more than 20 death threats during a bitter police pay dispute two years ago.
Former South Australian police minister Wayne Matthew said that in one incident at the height of the pay his wife was forced off the road by a police car.

"I can never accept the fact that my wife was forced off Lonsdale Road (in Adelaide) at 90 kms an hour, in broad daylight, by a marked police patrol car," Matthew told state parliament late on Tuesday.
"I can never accept that the police officers concerned gave her the traditional one-finger salute and skidded off in front of her," he added.

"I can never accept that my wife had to be the receiver of more than 20 phone calls -- death threats in fact -- levelled toward me during the time I was police minister, presiding over an industrial dispute....," he said.
Matthew said his wife Penny had been hospitalised for two weeks and required considerable counselling "as a result of the trauma she underwent at the time".
He said the government had not made public the incidents when they occurred because it did not wish to reflect unfairly on the majority of decent police.
He said believed appropriate internal action was taken by the police to stop the alleged harassment, although the department had been unable to identify the officers involved.
"(Politics) is a tough business...but you do not expect your family to also be victims," he said.
Police union official Peter Alexander said he found it extraordinary that the government had not made the allegations public nor taken the matter further at the time.
"If the allegations are true, it is outrageous behaviour, criminal behaviour and it would not be tolerated within the force or anywhere else," Alexander told ABC radio.
The state's police commisioner Mal Hyde was investigating the allegations, which were being taken very seriously, a spokeswoman said.
